notes: PUBLIC REFERENCE (this file): every port’s identity and coordinates, every link’s existence, operator and (where explicitly published) typical journey time, and every exchange rate’s value, all traced to a cited public source in each record’s `reference` field. See simulation/data/README-maritime.md for the full source list, licences and retrieval dates.

NOT PUBLIC REFERENCE (left to the simulation to synthesise): shipment capacity, cargo cost/pricing, produce-specific schedules or contracts, customs documentation/inspection/delay behaviour, weather delay, vessel positions, and any journey time not explicitly published (recorded here as null). A listed port or link is evidence that public transport infrastructure or a scheduled passenger service exists between two places — it is not proof that any produce-trading service exists on that route, and must not be treated as one.

Ports are keyed to the island ids in simulation/src/scenario/caribbean-islands-v1.ts (via caribbean-islands-manifest-v1.ts). All 28 manifest islands have at least one port; bonaire-sint-eustatius-saba, saint-kitts-nevis, trinidad-tobago and united-states-virgin-islands have more than one because those manifest island ids each cover multiple physically distinct islands.

Links only connect ports that are in this file’s own ports[] array. Two links (trinidad-tobago-intra and saint-kitts-nevis-intra) connect two ports that share the same manifest islandId — they document real intra-territory infrastructure but are not “inter-island” in the manifest-scope sense that issue #40 gates on; consumers that restrict routing to the selected run scope should treat a link’s relevance by whether its two ports’ islandIds are both in scope, which is trivially true for these two.

No island was found to have zero usable public-reference port; islands with no outgoing public-reference link at all (no scheduled ferry, cargo or cruise connection to another manifest island could be verified) are: antigua-barbuda, aruba, bahamas, barbados, cayman-islands, cuba, curacao, dominican-republic, grenada, haiti, jamaica, montserrat, puerto-rico, saint-barthelemy, saint-vincent-grenadines, turks-caicos-islands (16 of 28). This is a statement about what a public search could verify in this session, not proof that no such service exists.
